rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Maximum Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent only once each year by no more than 3% of current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less. The maximum allowable increase for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027 is 2.87 percent.
rules.key_value: lesser of 3% of current rent or 80% of CPI change
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord can only raise your rent by a certain amount each year. The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - Just Cause Evictions
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as not paying rent, breaking the lease, or the landlord moving into the property. For certain eviction reasons, the landlord may have to help pay the tenant's moving costs.
rules.citation: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
